sentence_stem: Had she known about the delay,
correct_completion: she would have taken an earlier train.
full_sentence: Had she known about the delay, she would have taken an earlier train.
acceptable_variants: she might have taken an earlier train.
she could have caught an earlier train.

options.text: she takes an earlier train every day.
options.why_wrong: The inverted 'had' structure sets up an unreal past condition, so the result must be a past conditional; a present habitual form does not fit.

options.text: she has known about the delay since morning.
options.why_wrong: This describes a state of knowledge but does not complete the unreal conditional result that 'had she known' requires.

options.text: she would have taken an earlier train.
she will have taken an earlier train.
options.why_wrong: The future perfect does not express the hypothetical past result required after an inverted third conditional.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (had + subject + past participle, with would have as the result)
explanation: In an inverted third conditional, 'had' replaces 'if' at the start of the clause. The main clause then needs 'would have' plus a past participle to show what would have happened in an unreal past situation. Spanish speakers often expect a simple past or a present form here, so it helps to focus on the 'would have' pattern.
translation: Si hubiera sabido del retraso, habría tomado un tren más temprano.
